emb:L2036057136.model_family: convolutional neural networks (various, across included studies)
emb:L2036057136.patient_population: children undergoing hand-wrist radiography for bone age assessment, pooled across 33 studies (2019-2024, mostly East Asian in-house cohorts)
emb:L2036057136.model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies applying AI/ML (mostly convolutional neural networks) to estimate bone age from pediatric hand-wrist radiographs, most using radiologist-annotated bone age rather than chronological age as ground truth. Pooled performance across studies reporting mean absolute error (MAE) was synthesized.
emb:L2036057136.dataset_size: 33 studies included; mostly in-house hand radiograph datasets from local populations
emb:L2036057136.headline_result: pooled weighted mean absolute error of 7.54 months for bone age estimation across included studies

emb:L2038240705.model_family: 3D convolutional neural network pretrained with polygenic scores, fine-tuned on diffusion MRI
emb:L2038240705.clinical_problem: prediction of youth depression and suicidality risk
emb:L2038240705.patient_population: multi-ethnic Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study cohort (N=4,741 for pretraining, N=266 for cross-sectional prediction), with independent validation in a Korean youth sample (N=108)
emb:L2038240705.model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network was pretrained on diffusion MRI (track-weighted fractional anisotropy) using polygenic depression risk scores to capture gene-brain associations in a multi-ethnic youth cohort, then fine-tuned to predict cross-sectional and two-year depression/suicidality outcomes. Explainable AI identified the superior longitudinal fasciculus, cingulum and corpus callosum as the most predictive white-matter tracts, and the model generalized to an independent Korean youth sample.
emb:L2038240705.dataset_size: 4,741 ABCD participants for pretraining; N=266 cross-sectional; independent validation N=108 Korean youth
emb:L2038240705.headline_result: cross-sectional AUC 0.62; two-year prediction of depression/suicidality AUC 0.61-0.66, up to 24% accuracy improvement over PGS-only and 5.8% over brain-only models; independent Korean validation AUC 0.67
emb:L2038240705.study_design: prospective cohort study with deep learning model development and external validation

emb:L2038112912.patient_population: fetuses/pregnant patients undergoing obstetric ultrasound and MRI
emb:L2038112912.model_description: Narrative review describing how AI has been applied to obstetric ultrasound examination, fetal heart monitoring, and MRI to improve diagnostic efficiency and accuracy. Does not describe a specific model, dataset, or quantitative result.

emb:L2038050518.model_family: support vector machine (linear kernel) on resting-state fMRI functional connectivity features
emb:L2038050518.clinical_problem: diagnosis of adolescent depression from brain functional connectivity
emb:L2038050518.patient_population: 94 adolescents with depression and 78 age- and gender-matched healthy adolescents, recruited at a single hospital's psychiatric imaging outpatient department
emb:L2038050518.model_description: Resting-state functional MRI was used to derive whole-brain network connectivity via group-level independent component analysis; top-ranked functional connectivity features between networks (sensorimotor, visual, auditory, default mode, cognitive control) were used to train a linear support vector machine classifying adolescents with depression versus healthy controls.
emb:L2038050518.headline_result: classification accuracy 70.35%, sensitivity 70.21%, specificity 71.80%, AUC 0.724 (95% CI 0.648-0.800) for diagnosing adolescent depression

emb:L2038239913.model_family: machine learning models combining multilevel/multidomain factors with structural and functional brain connectivity features
emb:L2038239913.clinical_problem: prediction of early alcohol use (sipping) trajectories in youth
emb:L2038239913.patient_population: youth from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study followed longitudinally for alcohol sipping behavior
emb:L2038239913.model_description: Machine learning models were applied to baseline individual, family and environmental factors together with structural and functional brain connectivity MRI features from the ABCD Study, analyzed separately and in combination, to prospectively predict longitudinal alcohol sipping trajectories in youth. Functional connectivity and multilevel factors distinguished youth on increasing versus decreasing sipping trajectories.
emb:L2038239913.dataset_size: large sample from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (exact n not given)
emb:L2038239913.headline_result: functional connectivity and multilevel factors distinguished youth with increasing versus decreasing alcohol sipping trajectories; no single accuracy/AUC figure given
emb:L2038239913.study_design: prospective cohort study using machine learning with explainable AI

emb:L2036600791.model_family: deep learning pipeline (nine models compared) with transfer learning for landmark segmentation and age estimation
emb:L2036600791.patient_population: 742 whole-body CT and 164 pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis CT scans, ages 1-60 years (437 male, 469 female), with fine-tuning and validation subgroups ages 15-35
emb:L2036600791.model_description: A deep learning pipeline segments the clavicle volume of interest on sternoclavicular joint CT and estimates chronological age, comparing nine deep learning models and using transfer learning fine-tuned on a smaller age group. The model also classifies age thresholds (over 14 and over 18 years) and ossification stage, and its performance was compared with age assessment by a radiologist and two forensic pathologists.
emb:L2036600791.dataset_size: 742 whole-body CT and 164 pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis CT scans (training); fine-tuning and validation groups of 10 scans each
emb:L2036600791.headline_result: mean absolute error 4.23 ± 4.49 years in cross-validation (3.30 ± 3.58 years after fine-tuning); AUC 0.99 for age classification (>14 and >18 years); accuracy 0.97 for ossification stage classification
emb:L2036600791.study_design: retrospective model development and validation study

emb:L2037625217.model_family: convolutional neural network using seed-based resting-state fMRI functional connectivity; compared with SVM and random forest
emb:L2037625217.clinical_problem: diagnosis of ADHD using brain functional connectivity
emb:L2037625217.patient_population: 776 subjects from the ADHD-200 Global Competition dataset, collected at three data centers, children being the study focus
emb:L2037625217.model_description: Seed-based correlation was used to extract functional connectivity features from resting-state fMRI focused on default mode network regions relevant to ADHD, and a convolutional neural network was trained to classify children with ADHD versus controls, benchmarked against an SVM and a random forest classifier on the public ADHD-200 dataset.
emb:L2037625217.dataset_size: 776 subjects from the ADHD-200 dataset (three data centers)
emb:L2037625217.headline_result: neural network classifier achieved 97% accuracy; SVM 83% accuracy; random forest 50% accuracy for ADHD classification
emb:L2037625217.study_design: retrospective classification model development using a public dataset

Does not report a single model, dataset, or fetal-imaging-specific quantitative figure.

emb:L2037612383.model_family: radiomics with LASSO feature selection and a nomogram combining radiomics score and MRI findings
emb:L2037612383.clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
emb:L2037612383.patient_population: 113 children with medulloblastoma and 31 children with ependymoma
emb:L2037612383.model_description: Radiomics features were extracted from ADC, T2WI and DCE-T1WI MRI sequences of children with posterior fossa tumors, and LASSO regression selected features to compute a radiomics score. A nomogram combining the radiomics score with MRI findings was built to differentiate medulloblastoma from ependymoma preoperatively, with single-sequence and combined-sequence models compared.
emb:L2037612383.dataset_size: 113 patients with medulloblastoma, 31 with ependymoma (144 total)
emb:L2037612383.headline_result: combined three-sequence radiomics nomogram achieved AUC 0.981 (primary cohort) and 0.939 (validation cohort); best single-sequence (ADC) model AUC 0.936/0.924

emb:L2037598989.model_family: unsupervised deep learning framework using two generative networks (image decomposition) with symmetry, adversarial and uniformity losses
emb:L2037598989.clinical_problem: correction of MRI intensity bias-field artifact to improve downstream image analysis
emb:L2037598989.patient_population: MRI datasets from healthy adults, brain tumor patients, infants, and mice (multi-population technical validation)
emb:L2037598989.model_description: An unsupervised deep learning framework decomposes a 3D brain MRI into a clean image and its bias field using two interacting generative networks, trained with a symmetry-based loss alongside adversarial and uniformity losses, without requiring matched clean/biased training pairs. It was evaluated on MRI from healthy adults, brain tumor patients, infants, and mice, and outperformed traditional and other deep learning bias-field correction methods.
emb:L2037598989.release_evidence: abstract states "the code will be made publicly available" (not yet available at time of publication)

emb:L2037732607.model_family: deep learning anatomical landmark localization on 3D slice-to-volume reconstructed MRI
emb:L2037732607.clinical_problem: automated fetal brain biometry reporting for prenatal assessment of brain maturation
emb:L2037732607.patient_population: fetuses at 20-40 weeks gestation undergoing 3D T2-weighted fetal brain MRI; retrospective evaluation on 90 cases, prospective evaluation on 111 cases across varied gestational ages, field strengths and scan parameters; normative centiles from 406 normal controls (19-40 weeks)
emb:L2037732607.model_description: Deep learning models localize 13 routinely reported linear fetal brain biometry landmarks on 3D slice-to-volume-reconstructed T2-weighted MRI, automatically computing measurements and growth centiles and generating an html report, removing reliance on manual 2D measurements that are affected by fetal motion and inconsistent plane selection. The fully automated pipeline was evaluated retrospectively and prospectively across a wide range of scanners and gestational ages.
emb:L2037732607.dataset_size: 90 retrospective cases, 111 prospective cases, 406 normal controls for centile charts
emb:L2037732607.headline_result: more than 98% of landmark placements graded acceptable in prospective evaluation; automated vs. manual measurement difference within 1-3mm; processing time under 5 minutes per case
emb:L2037732607.study_design: retrospective and prospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2037380108.model_family: machine learning model using structural connectome gradient features
emb:L2037380108.clinical_problem: prediction of later cognitive ability (IQ) from early brain structural connectivity
emb:L2037380108.patient_population: children with structural connectome gradients measured by MRI at age 1, followed to assess IQ in early and middle childhood
emb:L2037380108.model_description: Structural connectome gradients, representing continuous spatial variation in brain structural connectivity, were derived from MRI acquired at age 1. Machine learning was used to predict future intelligence quotient (IQ) in early and middle childhood from these gradient features, testing whether early structural organization relates to later cognitive variability.
emb:L2037380108.study_design: prospective cohort study using machine learning

emb:L2037354810.model_family: quantized variational autoencoder with multi-head attention conditioning (3D CNN and transformer), contrastive learning
emb:L2037354810.clinical_problem: early diagnosis of cerebral palsy via multi-contrast MRI slice-thickness synthesis
emb:L2037354810.patient_population: children requiring multi-contrast MRI for cerebral palsy diagnosis, for whom deep, thin-slice acquisition is limited by uncooperative movement
emb:L2037354810.model_description: CaT-MDT takes thick-slice, lower-resolution multi-contrast MRI (e.g. T1, T2, FLAIR) from children, who often cannot tolerate long high-resolution scans, and synthesizes thinner-slice, higher-information images while limiting partial-volume effects. It uses a quantized variational autoencoder with attention conditioned on the desired slice depth and contrastive learning across modalities of the same subject, aiming to retain lesion and biological trait information (age, sex, weight) to support cerebral palsy diagnosis and lesion identification.
emb:L2037354810.headline_result: translation quality MAE 0.159, SSIM 0.988, PSNR 63.13; higher cerebral palsy prediction scores at multiple slice-depth translation levels

emb:L2037732324.model_family: deep learning segmentation models (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) plus a segmentation-free classifier with segmentation-informed pretraining
emb:L2037732324.clinical_problem: non-invasive prediction of BRAF mutation status in pediatric low-grade glioma
emb:L2037732324.patient_population: 455 patients with molecularly-characterized pediatric low-grade glioma treated between 1999 and 2023 at a single tertiary care children's hospital
emb:L2037732324.model_description: Whole-brain FLAIR MRI from children with low-grade glioma was used to train and compare three medical image segmentation models (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet), then a segmentation-free classifier was developed to predict BRAF status directly from the whole-brain FLAIR sequence without relying on any manual or automated segmentation, using a pretraining strategy that embeds segmentation knowledge into the classifier. Performance was compared with a baseline model using manual tumor segmentations as input.
emb:L2037732324.headline_result: MedNeXt segmentation Dice 0.555 (best of three models); segmentation-free classifier AUC 0.741 for BRAF status, improved to 0.772 with segmentation-informed pretraining, not significantly different from the manual-segmentation baseline (0.756, p=0.141)

emb:L2037809904.patient_population: children aged 0-6 months undergoing hip ultrasound screening

emb:L2036994902.model_family: CNN-transformer hybrid with localized attention mechanisms
emb:L2036994902.body_region: fetal anatomy (maternal-fetal planes, including fetal brain)
emb:L2036994902.clinical_problem: classification of maternal-fetal ultrasound anatomical planes and anomaly detection
emb:L2036994902.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing maternal-fetal ultrasound; real-world clinical dataset collected from multiple practitioners and equipment types
emb:L2036994902.model_description: Conv-LAMAP combines convolutional neural networks with transformer-based localized attention to classify maternal-fetal ultrasound anatomical planes and detect anomalies, and is also applied to fine-grained categorization of fetal brain images for autism-related structural patterns. It was trained and evaluated on a real-world clinical ultrasound dataset from multiple practitioners and equipment types, compared against other CNN architectures and a related model (CageVIT).
emb:L2036994902.study_design: technical development and comparative evaluation study

emb:L2037301014.model_family: elastic-net penalized linear regression on MRI radiomic features
emb:L2037301014.clinical_problem: prediction of 18-month neurodevelopmental outcome after perinatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE)
emb:L2037301014.patient_population: 160 neonates with gestational age ≥35 weeks and neonatal encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia at a quaternary neonatal neurocritical care unit, born 2018-2022
emb:L2037301014.model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from deep-gray matter structures and 2,224 whole-brain image tiles on MRI obtained on postnatal day 4-5 after therapeutic hypothermia in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. These features were input to an elastic-net penalized linear regression model, evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation, to predict cognitive, language and motor developmental outcomes at 18 months (Bayley Scales), and predictor weights were mapped back into brain regions.
emb:L2037301014.headline_result: mean correlation between predicted and observed 18-month Bayley outcomes 0.947; mean coefficient of determination 0.879 across cognitive, language and motor domains (10-fold cross-validation)
emb:L2037301014.study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study with cross-validated model development

emb:L2037096921.model_family: nine machine learning models compared (logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, k-nearest neighbor, SVM, naive Bayes, gradient boosting machine, LightGBM, XGBoost) on MRI radiomics features
emb:L2037096921.clinical_problem: prediction of cerebral palsy risk in infants
emb:L2037096921.patient_population: 178 infants aged 4 months to 2 years (89 cerebral palsy, 89 non-cerebral palsy controls), single center; training set n=142, test set n=36
emb:L2037096921.model_description: T1- and T2-weighted MRI from infants aged 4 months to 2 years was segmented and 11,190 radiomics features extracted per patient; after feature selection (t-test, LASSO, Z-score normalization), nine machine learning algorithms were trained to predict cerebral palsy risk, with performance compared by ROC analysis and the best model further evaluated with five-fold cross-validation.
emb:L2037096921.dataset_size: 178 infants (89 cerebral palsy, 89 non-cerebral palsy controls); training set n=142, test set n=36
emb:L2037096921.headline_result: logistic regression model had the best and most stable performance, AUC 0.971 (training) and 0.963 (test), sensitivity/specificity/accuracy approximately 0.93-0.94
emb:L2037096921.study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic modeling study

emb:L2037285074.model_family: automated AI-based brain segmentation technique for regional volumetry
emb:L2037285074.clinical_problem: characterization of brain structural differences in autism spectrum disorder using automated volumetric segmentation
emb:L2037285074.patient_population: 52 children with autism spectrum disorder (DSM-5 diagnosed) and 48 age- and gender-matched typically developing children, single hospital in Qingdao, China, January 2023-April 2024
emb:L2037285074.model_description: 3D T1-weighted 3.0T MRI was obtained from children with autism spectrum disorder and typically developing controls. An automated AI-based brain segmentation technique computed standardized volumes for individual brain structures as a fraction of whole-brain volume, which were compared between groups and correlated with Gesell Developmental Scale scores.
emb:L2037285074.dataset_size: 52 children with ASD, 48 typically developing controls (100 total)
emb:L2037285074.headline_result: ASD group showed significantly increased volumes in grey matter, orbitofrontal cortex, hippocampus and several other regions and decreased pericalcarine cortex/posterior corpus callosum volume (all P<0.05); right thalamus volume negatively correlated with Gesell adaptation quotient (r=-0.276, P=0.048)

emb:L2037300781.exclusion_reason: Chest X-ray classification model for pneumonia, tuberculosis and normal/non-X-ray images; the training dataset's pediatric status is not stated, children are mentioned only as background epidemiology

emb:L2031007817.model_family: deep learning models (rod model, 58 mm reference model, head-piece model) for landmark detection and measurement
emb:L2031007817.clinical_problem: automated measurement of growing rod length in children with early-onset scoliosis treated with magnetically controlled growing rods
emb:L2031007817.patient_population: children with early-onset scoliosis treated with magnetically controlled growing rods; 387 radiographs used for model development and 60 radiographs (118 rods) for final testing
emb:L2031007817.model_description: Three deep learning models (rod model, 58 mm reference-marker model, head-piece model) were developed to automatically detect landmarks on posteroanterior spine radiographs and calculate the adjusted length of magnetically controlled growing rods in children with early-onset scoliosis, replacing subjective and time-consuming manual measurement.
emb:L2031007817.dataset_size: 387 radiographs for development, 60 radiographs (118 rods) for testing
emb:L2031007817.headline_result: average precision 67.6%/94.8%/86.3% for the three models; mean absolute difference of rod length change 0.98 ± 0.88 mm vs. manual measurement, inter-method correlation coefficient 0.90; average processing time 6.1 seconds per measurement

emb:L2032795091.clinical_problem: super-resolution reconstruction of ultra-low-field MRI to improve paediatric neurodevelopmental imaging in low-resource settings
emb:L2032795091.patient_population: infants scanned with paired ultra-low-field and high-field MRI
emb:L2032795091.model_description: A deep learning 'multi-orientation U-Net' takes multiple low-resolution, anisotropic T2-weighted images acquired on an ultra-low-field MRI scanner in orthogonal orientations and reconstructs a single high-resolution isotropic image, aiming to improve MRI accessibility in low- and middle-income countries where high-field scanners are unavailable. It was trained and evaluated on paired ultra-low-field and high-field infant brain MRI data.
emb:L2032795091.headline_result: improved deep brain structure (caudate) volume estimation versus prior state-of-the-art methods: linear correlation r=0.94 (vs. 0.84), concordance correlation 0.94 (vs. 0.80), mean error 0.05 cm3 (vs. 0.36 cm3)

emb:L2034173687.exclusion_reason: fNIRS study of Theory of Mind/scalar-implicature brain networks in children and adults; a cognitive-neuroscience activation study, not an AI/ML diagnostic model for a clinical question

emb:L2034447972.model_family: convolutional neural network with ensemble learning
emb:L2034447972.body_region: fetal anatomy (abdomen, brain, femur, thorax, maternal cervix)
emb:L2034447972.clinical_problem: automatic classification of standard fetal ultrasound planes
emb:L2034447972.model_description: An end-to-end automatic system using convolutional neural networks with ensemble learning classifies fetal ultrasound images into six categories (abdomen, brain, femur, thorax, maternal cervix, other planes), aiming to reduce the time and effort of manual plane identification and improve robustness and accuracy of standard-plane detection.

emb:L2036065649.model_family: InceptionV3 (deep learning CNN, transfer learning), compared against other deep learning models
emb:L2036065649.clinical_problem: differentiating atelectasis from consolidation on pediatric chest radiographs
emb:L2036065649.patient_population: pediatric patients: 1,297 chest radiographs (500 with consolidation, 499 with atelectasis, 298 without opacities)
emb:L2036065649.model_description: A deep learning classification model was trained on 1,297 pediatric chest radiographs labeled as consolidation, atelectasis, or no opacity, to help differentiate types of non-interstitial opacity that can otherwise be difficult to distinguish given the overlapping symptomatology of pediatric respiratory disease. The InceptionV3 architecture performed best among the deep learning models tested, intended to assist radiologists supporting pediatricians in diagnosis.
emb:L2036065649.dataset_size: 1,297 chest radiographs (500 consolidation, 499 atelectasis, 298 without opacities)
emb:L2036065649.study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation study

emb:L2036077143.clinical_problem: quality assessment and interpretation of 4D fetal facial ultrasound imaging
emb:L2036077143.patient_population: fetuses undergoing four-dimensional (4D) ultrasound for fetal facial imaging
emb:L2036077143.model_description: Literature review of machine learning and deep learning algorithms applied to four-dimensional fetal facial ultrasound, covering automated detection and segmentation of anatomical structures within the fetal face, scan quality assessment, and multitask/transfer learning strategies developed to address variable convergence rates and limited training data. Does not describe a single named model or quantitative results.

emb:L2036886893.clinical_problem: improving detection and diagnosis of congenital heart disease via automated, standardized fetal echocardiography
emb:L2036886893.patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography for congenital heart disease screening and diagnosis
emb:L2036886893.model_description: Narrative review of AI applications in fetal echocardiography, covering automated image acquisition and optimization, automatic biometric measurement, identification of discrepant values, and diagnosis/classification of congenital heart disease, aiming to standardize examinations, reduce variation in detection rates between regions, and reduce reliance on operator experience. emb:L2037218144.model_family: Vision Transformer (ViT), Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT), Vision-LSTM (ViL), Multi-axis Vision Transformer (MaxViT)
emb:L2037218144.clinical_problem: classification of standard fetal cardiac ultrasound views
emb:L2037218144.patient_population: 200 normal fetuses at 18 to 24+6 weeks gestation undergoing fetal cardiac ultrasound; training set n=140, test set n=60
emb:L2037218144.model_description: Four deep learning architectures (ViT, DeiT, ViL, MaxViT) were trained and compared for classifying seven standard fetal cardiac ultrasound views (three-vessel and trachea, apical four-chamber, aortic arch long-axis, bicaval, LVOT, three-vessel, RVOT) in 200 normal fetuses.
